sub_theme: Traditional Tales: Goldilocks and the Three Bears

lessons.title: Story Time: Goldilocks and the Three Bears
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify the four main characters and the setting.
lessons.starter_activity: Predict the story from the cover.
lessons.main_activity: Read/tell the story with expression using different voices for each bear (big, medium, small).

differentiation.extension: Predict what Goldilocks will find next

lessons.assessment_notes: Note character/setting recall — evidence for LIT.1.
lessons.plenary: Recap the three bears and Goldilocks together.
lessons.home_link: Retell the story to someone at home.

lessons.title: Big, Medium, Small: Ordering by Size
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to order three objects by size using comparative language.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the three bears' sizes from the story.
lessons.main_activity: Children order three bowls/chairs/beds (props or pictures) from smallest to biggest, using size vocabulary.
resources_needed: Three sizes of bowls/chairs pictures or props

differentiation.extension: Order and explain reasoning for all 3

lessons.assessment_notes: Note size-ordering skill — evidence for MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Class recap using big/medium/small vocabulary.
lessons.home_link: Order 3 objects by size at home.

lessons.title: Where Do Bears Live?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe where real bears live and what they eat.
lessons.starter_activity: Compare the storybook bears to real bears (pictures).
lessons.main_activity: Discuss real bear facts (forest habitats, hibernation, diet) using picture/video resources.

differentiation.support: Share one simple fact with support

lessons.assessment_notes: Note factual recall about real animals — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Recap real bear facts learned.
lessons.home_link: Look up a fact about a woodland animal together.

lessons.title: Making the Three Bears' Porridge Bowls
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to create three different-sized bowls using craft materials.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the porridge scene from the story.
lessons.main_activity: Children make three paper/card bowls in different sizes representing each bear's porridge bowl.
key_questions: How did you make it a different size?

differentiation.extension: Cut own shapes in three distinct sizes

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe size discrimination and fine motor skill — evidence for EAD.1/MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Display the three bowls in size order.
lessons.home_link: Find three different-sized bowls/cups at home and order them.

lessons.title: Phonics: Introducing 'b'
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to say the sound 'b' and blend words (bed, big, bag).
lessons.starter_activity: Recap sounds learned so far.
lessons.main_activity: Introduce 'b' sound/action; blend new CVC words.
lessons.assessment_notes: Update phonics tracker for 'b'.
lessons.plenary: Sing all 16 sounds learned.
lessons.home_link: Practise blending bed, big, bag.

lessons.title: Counting Porridge Spoonfuls
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count a given number of 'spoonfuls' accurately up to 10.
lessons.starter_activity: Count claps representing spoonfuls together.
lessons.main_activity: Children use a spoon to 'serve' a counted number of pretend porridge (pom poms) into bowls, checking accuracy.
key_questions: How many spoonfuls did you count?
Can you count them again to check?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record counting accuracy — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Class total count recap.
lessons.home_link: Count spoonfuls while helping serve food at home.

lessons.title: Tasting Porridge: Hot, Warm, Cold
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe temperature differences using appropriate vocabulary.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap 'too hot, too cold, just right' from the story.
lessons.main_activity: (Allergy-checked, cooled to safe temps) children compare warm and cold porridge samples safely, describing temperature differences.
resources_needed: Cooled porridge samples at different safe temperatures
key_questions: How can you tell without touching?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note temperature vocabulary and safe observation — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Recap 'just right' and why Goldilocks liked it.
lessons.home_link: Talk about hot and cold foods/drinks at home safely.

lessons.title: Role-Play: Goldilocks and the Three Bears
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to act out a scene using different-sized voices for each character.
lessons.starter_activity: Practise a big deep voice and a small squeaky voice.
lessons.main_activity: In small groups, children act out the 'who's been sitting in my chair' scene using different voices for each bear.
key_questions: What does the big bear say?
How does Goldilocks feel when she wakes up?
lessons.assessment_notes: Observe expressive voice use and confidence — evidence for EAD.2/CL.2.
lessons.plenary: One group performs for the class.
lessons.home_link: Act out the story with different voices at home.

lessons.title: Retelling Using a Story Map
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use a story map to retell key events in order.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a simple story map of Goldilocks together.
lessons.main_activity: In pairs, children use a story map (porridge, chairs, beds, waking up) to retell the story in sequence.
key_questions: What happened when the bears came home?

differentiation.support: Retell with adult prompting at each stage

lessons.assessment_notes: Note sequencing and retelling ability — evidence for LIT.1/CL.2.
lessons.plenary: One pair retells to the class using the map.
lessons.home_link: Retell the story using a simple story map at home.

lessons.title: Matching Chairs, Bowls, and Beds to the Right Bear
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to match objects of corresponding size to the correct character.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the three bears' relative sizes.
lessons.main_activity: Children match sets of differently-sized chair/bowl/bed picture cards to the correct bear character.
key_questions: How do you know it belongs to the small bear?

differentiation.extension: Match all 3 sets (chairs, bowls, beds) independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note size-matching and reasoning skill — evidence for MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of all correct matches.
lessons.home_link: Match items of different sizes at home to their correct owner (e.g. family shoes).

lessons.title: Whose Things Are These? Belongings and Respect
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to explain why it's important to ask before using someone else's things.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss how the bears might have felt about Goldilocks using their things without asking.
lessons.main_activity: Class discussion about respecting others' belongings and asking permission, linked to the story's events.
key_questions: How did the bears feel when they came home?
Why should we ask before using someone's things?

differentiation.extension: Explain reasoning about respect and permission

lessons.assessment_notes: Note social understanding — evidence for UTW.2/PSED.3.
lessons.plenary: Class agreement: 'always ask before borrowing.'
lessons.home_link: Practise asking permission before using a family member's things.

lessons.title: Three Bears Family Portrait Craft
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to represent three different-sized bear characters using craft materials.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at pictures of the three bears together.
lessons.main_activity: Children create a family portrait of the three bears using different-sized paper circles/shapes for bodies and heads.
resources_needed: Brown paper circles in 3 sizes, craft materials
key_questions: How did you show the size difference?

differentiation.extension: Cut own shapes and add detailed features

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe size discrimination and craft skill — evidence for EAD.1/MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Display the three bears family portraits.
lessons.home_link: Draw your own family showing different sizes at home.

lessons.title: Writing 'Too Hot, Too Cold, Just Right' Labels
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to attempt to write a simple descriptive label.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the repeated phrase pattern in the story.
lessons.main_activity: Children draw three bowls and attempt to write 'hot', 'cold', 'just right' labels using known phonics sounds.
key_questions: What word will you write for this bowl?
What sound does it start with?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note purposeful writing attempt — evidence for LIT.3.
lessons.plenary: Share labelled bowls with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Label hot/cold items at home with help.

lessons.title: One More/One Less with Porridge Bowls
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to find one more or one less than a number up to 5 using porridge counters.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap one more/one less from Week 2.
lessons.main_activity: Using pom pom 'porridge' counters, children practise one more/one less questions in a story context.
key_questions: What is one more than 3 spoonfuls?

differentiation.support: Use physical counters and count aloud

lessons.assessment_notes: Record confidence with one more/one less — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Quick-fire one more/one less game.
lessons.home_link: Practise one more/one less with snacks at home.

lessons.title: Materials Recap: Comparing Chairs (Hard vs Soft)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare and describe object properties (hard, soft, comfortable).
lessons.starter_activity: Recap why Goldilocks preferred the small chair.
lessons.main_activity: Children test sitting on/feeling different textured chairs/cushions, describing hard vs soft using vocabulary.
resources_needed: Variety of chairs/cushions with different textures
lessons.assessment_notes: Note descriptive material vocabulary — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Recap hard/soft vocabulary learned.
lessons.home_link: Compare hard and soft surfaces at home.

lessons.title: Composing a 'Who's Been Sitting in My Chair' Chant
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to join in with and adapt a repeated story phrase as a chant.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the repeated phrase from the story.
lessons.main_activity: As a class, practise the chant with actions and big/medium/small voice changes, then create a new verse.
key_questions: Can you say it in a big bear voice?
Can you think of a new line?

differentiation.support: Join in with voice changes only

lessons.assessment_notes: Note creative contribution and voice control — evidence for EAD.2/CL.2.
lessons.plenary: Perform the chant together with all voice variations.
lessons.home_link: Perform the chant for family using different voices.

lessons.title: Retelling the Whole Story Independently
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retell Goldilocks and the Three Bears with beginning, middle, and end.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's learning about the story.
lessons.main_activity: In small groups, children retell the full story using puppets/props and their story maps from Wednesday.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note full narrative retelling ability — evidence for LIT.1/CL.2.
lessons.plenary: One group performs their retelling to the class.
lessons.home_link: Retell the whole story to your family this weekend.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Counting, Size, One More/Less
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply counting, size-ordering, and one more/less skills from this week.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's maths vocabulary.
lessons.main_activity: Rotate through 3 stations: counting porridge spoonfuls, size ordering (chairs/bowls/beds), one more/one less.
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 9 maths observations.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising size ordering and counting over the weekend.

lessons.title: Bears and Belongings Recap Display
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key learning about bears, materials, and respecting belongings.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's UTW learning.
lessons.main_activity: Contribute to a class display summarising bear facts, hard/soft comparisons, and the importance of respecting belongings.
key_questions: What did we learn about bears?
What did we learn about respecting things?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning — evidence for UTW.3/UTW.2.
lessons.plenary: Unveil and admire the finished display.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about bears and respect with your family.

lessons.title: Goldilocks Performance Celebration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to perform the story as a class with confidence using props, chant, and voices.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all elements learned this week (voices, chant, bowls).
lessons.main_activity: Whole-class performance of Goldilocks combining role-play, the chant, and the craft bowls/portraits as props.
key_questions: What was your favourite part of the story week?
How did it feel to perform?
lessons.assessment_notes: Observe confidence and enjoyment across the week's story learning — evidence for EAD.2/CL.2.
lessons.plenary: Round of applause; recap the fun traditional tales week.
lessons.home_link: Perform part of the story for family this weekend.
